Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise while pregnant; could you please tell me how many weeks pregnant you are and when these symptoms started?

To help narrow this down, has anyone in your household or close contact circle become ill recently, and have you traveled anywhere or consumed specific foods like unpasteurized dairy?

Given your third-trimester status and symptoms of fever, headache, and malaise, have you experienced any visual disturbances like blurred vision or scotomas, or any sudden swelling in your hands and face? speaker: Doctor
text:
With the negative urine protein and normal liver function tests, pre-eclampsia is unlikely. To distinguish between a viral infection like West Nile virus or other causes, have you noticed any severe muscle weakness, tingling sensations in your limbs, or any changes in your mental status?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Viral Syndrome in Pregnancy (likely viral etiology given negative specific tests and lack of focal neurological findings).

I have exhausted my questions and tests. The normal liver function tests, negative urine protein, negative skin exam, and normal CSF/West Nile results effectively rule out pre-eclampsia, hepatitis, meningococcemia, and West Nile virus. Your symptoms are most consistent with a non-specific viral infection common in pregnancy.
